attempts.summary: Deployed inventory-api as an OpenRC-managed service on node1 (Alpine 3.23) with kernel OOM protection: a Python/sqlite HTTP service (/health, GET+POST /inventory) runs as an unprivileged 'inventory' user under /etc/init.d/inventory-api, added to the default runlevel, with a start_post hook that sets its oom_score_adj to -1000. Verified end-to-end: launched an unrelated memory-hog process (oom_score_adj=1000) that drove the node's ~2GB RAM (no swap) to exhaustion; dmesg confirmed the kernel OOM killer selected and killed only the hog (pid 3202), while inventory-api (pid 3096, oom_score_adj=-1000) was left untouched and continued serving reads and writes throughout and after the event. Completed the mandatory single-node restart protocol: captured boot_id b0ab50e6-fe4e-4dc1-ab2c-8418e85b41da plus healthy service/data state, issued a native `reboot`, polled through the outage, confirmed the changed boot_id (f55da554-70f8-4794-80cf-8dd032a1c84d), and verified inventory-api auto-started, re-applied its -1000 OOM protection, and served the same persisted data (including the item written after the OOM event) after recovery.
